chunks: ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Aṭiyyah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
When you have finished saying salām to the martyrs, you come to the grave of al-Ḥusayn, then you place it before you, then you pray as much as seems good to you.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper method for performing prayers at the grave of Imam al-Husayn according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the grave of Imam al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) as a primary locus for *Salat al-Ziyarah*, emphasizing the spiritual hierarchy where greetings to the broader martyrs precede the specific veneration of the Imam. By directing the visitor to face the grave and pray voluntarily, it underscores the concept of the Imam as an intercessor and a spiritual axis (*axis mundi*) connecting the earthly pilgrim to the divine presence.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Aťiyyah, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said (as part of a longer Ḥadīth):
After saying Salām to the martyrs, come (back) to the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) and face the grave and establish as many prayers as possible.
